name: Grain Swap — Live Viability-Driven Switch
description: Fig 5 as a fully runnable temporal study: a cell's viability is driven down by an external stress ramp (StressRamp); a GrainSelector swaps the active grain as viability crosses a threshold — while viable the COARSE grain grows the cell's biomass (linear yield), and once viability falls below the threshold the FINE grain takes over the dying regime, where biomass stops growing and DECAYS first-order. Exactly one grain runs per tick, so the coarse→fine switch — growth turning over to decline — plays out on-screen as viability slides. Low viability → fine grain.
